_source: Merged 27 Nov 2026: Team P6/P7 approved FAQ (waypoint ai_data.js, approved by the coordinator persona 20 Nov) + P01–P03 approved FAQ (ipp data/faq.txt). P01–P03 entry "Does applying mean I got the placement?" folded into FAQ-02 as a phrasing. Alternatives and keywords for FAQ-13..19 were added for retrieval; the approved answers are unchanged.

entries.question: How are internships recommended to me?
alternatives: Which internships fit me?
How does matching work?
Why was this opportunity suggested?
How do you rank opportunities?
What roles match my profile and skills?
entries.answer: The matching page suggests up to three open opportunities. It ranks them on four inputs you can see: required skills, desirable skills, shared interests and preferred location. Eligibility (programme, dates, listing open) is checked separately, and each suggestion lists its reasons and any skill gap. A suggestion is not an application or a placement.
entries.source: Binder P05: purpose and acceptance 1–2; Lab 3 matching guidance

entries.question: Who approves my placement?
alternatives: Is a recommendation an offer?
Does a match mean I got the internship?
Who confirms the placement?
Who signs off my internship?
Does applying mean I got the placement?
entries.answer: A recommendation is decision support only. A placement becomes official only after the employer makes an offer and the university confirms it; P04 then sends the placement with status university_confirmed. The co-op coordinator records that confirmation. The assistant and the matching engine cannot approve anything.
entries.source: Binder shared data (P04 placement record); Lab 3 human control

entries.question: How do I close a skill gap such as Jira?
alternatives: I am missing a required skill, what do I do?
How can I learn Jira?
How do I get better at a skill?
What should I do about a skill gap?
entries.answer: Open your preparation plan. Each gap links to a short module: read the resource, complete the practical task, and submit evidence with an explanation. A reviewer checks it against the module checklist. The gap closes only when the reviewer records the skill as demonstrated.

entries.question: Does finishing the module mean I have the skill?
alternatives: If I complete the reading, is my skill demonstrated?
Is reading the resource enough?
Do I get the skill after the course?
entries.answer: No. Completing the resource is recorded as activity only. A skill counts as demonstrated only after you submit evidence and a reviewer records the outcome against the checklist.

entries.question: What evidence do I need for the Jira module?
alternatives: What will the reviewer check?
What does the reviewer look for?
What is on the Jira checklist?
How is my Jira task assessed?
entries.answer: The reviewer checks four things: at least two work items with clear summaries; an owner on every item; at least one item moved from To do through In progress to Done; and a plain-language reason for each status change. Submit the board with an explanation of at least 25 words.

entries.question: What happens if the reviewer asks for a revision?
alternatives: My evidence was sent back
How do I resubmit?
The reviewer requested changes
entries.answer: Read the reviewer's comment on the module page, update your board or explanation, and submit again. Your original submission and the comment stay in the history, and the reviewer checks the new version against the same checklist.

entries.question: What is the learning agreement and who signs it?
alternatives: How do I set my co-op goals?
Who agrees my learning goals?
What goes in the learning agreement?
entries.answer: The learning agreement holds three of your goals, each mapped to at least one learning outcome. You, your workplace supervisor and your academic advisor each agree it; once all three have agreed, it is locked.

entries.question: How do I submit a weekly logbook entry?
alternatives: How do I record what I learned this week?
Where do I write my weekly log?
What does my supervisor do with my log?
entries.answer: Open the logbook, choose the goal the entry supports, describe what you did and learned (at least eight words) and link evidence if you have it. Your supervisor can acknowledge it or ask for more detail; if they ask, you revise it and the original stays in the history.

entries.question: How is my final review decided?
alternatives: Who grades my co-op?
How is my co-op assessed at the end?
Does my employer give my grade?
entries.answer: At the end of the period your employer gives feedback and your academic advisor records a separate academic judgement for each outcome. An outcome can be marked achieved only with evidence from that period. Official grading is outside this prototype and follows university process.
entries.source: Binder P07: acceptance 4; outside scope (official grading)

entries.question: Can I see other students' profiles?
alternatives: Can I look at a classmate's matches?
Show me another student's data
Who can see my records?
entries.answer: No. You can see only your own records. Coordinators and reviewers see what their role needs. This classroom demo uses synthetic students only, never real student information.
entries.source: Binder common terms (synthetic data); Lab 3 acceptance (no unapproved personal data)

entries.question: Why does my match say eligibility needs checking?
alternatives: My availability is missing
What does unknown eligibility mean?
Why is a condition unknown?
entries.answer: A mandatory condition could not be confirmed, usually because your availability dates are missing. The match is shown, but the condition is never treated as satisfied. Update your profile (P01) or ask the coordinator, who checks eligibility separately.

entries.question: Can I challenge a recommendation?
alternatives: I think my match is wrong
I disagree with my ranking
How do I ask the coordinator about a match?
entries.answer: Yes. On the matching page choose “Ask coordinator to review” on any suggestion and say why. The coordinator can question or correct the inputs and replies in the same record.
entries.source: Binder P05: acceptance 3 (how users can challenge a result)

entries.question: Are placements on site?
alternatives: Can I intern remotely?
Can I work from home?
Are remote internships allowed?
entries.answer: Yes. Placements are on site; remote roles are not approved.

entries.question: Can I work abroad?
alternatives: Can I do my internship overseas?
Is an internship in another country allowed?
entries.answer: It is difficult to approve. Exceptions are reviewed case by case by the coordinator.

entries.question: Who enters my final grade?
alternatives: Who gives my internship grade?
Who marks my co-op?
entries.answer: The faculty member assigned to your internship.

entries.question: What must an employer include?
alternatives: What information does an employer need to submit?
What goes in an opportunity submission?
entries.answer: Title, dates, location, work mode, a named supervisor, required skills, and the learning opportunities.

entries.question: How is an opportunity approved?
alternatives: How does the coordinator review a listing?
What is on the review checklist?
entries.answer: The coordinator checks it against a review checklist: completeness, on-site, duration, supervisor, learning value, employer reliability, and workplace safety.

entries.question: Why was my opportunity returned?
alternatives: My listing was sent back, why?
Why did the coordinator return my listing?
entries.answer: The reason is shown on its status. Fix the issue and resubmit.

entries.question: How do I resubmit?
alternatives: How do I send a corrected listing?
Can I submit a new version of my opportunity?
entries.answer: Submit a new version. The old version is kept and never overwritten.

_sensitive_note: Topics no approved entry covers go to the coordinator. remote/abroad were removed because P01–P03 approved answers now cover them (FAQ-13, FAQ-14).
